- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.50) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price dropped sharply.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3%.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7–10 day window.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early days (first 5–7) when sentiment is bullish; dampen initial forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.50 → +0.67), model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment momentum as signal for correction.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 73→65→62), model often holds too high; apply downward bias in 10–15 day horizon.
